**Deliberate non-merges**

E-018 and E-019 remain separate because excessive Invoice quantity and duplicate Invoice are different failures.

E-020 and E-021 remain separate because raising a Sales Credit Note and allocating a Customer Credit Note across Invoices are different permissions.

E-022 and E-023 remain separate because a signed Delivery Note photo and a goods photo use different delivery conditions.

E-045, E-046 and E-073 remain separate because overdue Invoice, near-expiry stock and Friday Statement of Account have different triggers and recipients.

E-064 to E-067 remain separate in the extraction record because each SQL write-back requires a separate field boundary, even though Part B retains the existing AUTO-11 umbrella ID.

E-093 was not merged into E-058; it contradicts the earlier Sales Order amendment design and therefore remains a competing proposal under AUTO-13 and DECISION-25.

**Coverage sweep result**

**Accounts:** Seven named people have evidenced responsibilities: David, Apple, CJ, Ben or Arben, Queenie, Grace and Lai. Warehouse workers, drivers and both backups remain unresolved. The minimum named count is 7; final total not evidenced.

**Roles and standard MAIA mappings:** Proposed mappings are David → Sales Master Manager; CJ → Sales Manager; Ben or Arben and Queenie → Sales User; Lai → Logistics Manager; warehouse workers → Logistics User; Grace → Finance Manager; Apple → Finance Master Manager; driver → Driver. System Manager holder is unresolved. All mappings are Proposed for Product confirmation.

**Price control:** David is client-stated as the price maintainer. Permission to approve below-minimum prices and CJ's narrower authority remain unresolved. Proposed gate roles: David and possibly CJ as Price Controller according to the final decisions.

**Credit control:** Salespeople cannot change credit limits. The person who sets limits and releases a blocked document remains unresolved among David, CJ and Apple.

**System administration:** David and Apple were discussed as broad administrators, then the client asked to review the arrangement. System Manager is not assigned.

**Document permissions:** See the full table below.

**Screen-level finance and CRM questions:** See the separate table below.

**Information restrictions:** Salespeople cannot change Customer credit limits. Other-salesperson Customer access and warehouse cost/Purchasing restrictions remain unresolved; nothing else is granted by silence.

**Notifications and channels:** Overdue-Invoice and near-expiry recipients were stated, but thresholds and channels are missing. Other notifications are Derived or Proposed. No final channel is confirmed; current operations use WhatsApp and UAT used Telegram.

**Warnings and stops:** Sales cannot change Customer credit limits; unclear payment matches require Finance selection. Invoice quantity and duplicate-Invoice protections were requested but may be standard. Credit, price and picked-variance intervention remain unresolved.

**Automatic actions:** SQL-agent assignment and fallback to David are client-stated. Draft Sales Order preparation, bulk price update, payment suggestions, quantity calculation and SQL updates remain Derived or Proposed.

**Existing-system sync:** SQL is the existing system. Customer and Item information flow SQL → MAIA. Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice and Payment Receipt are proposed MAIA → SQL after confirmation. Goods Receipt remains in SQL. No unit, warehouse or category-code translation table was found.

**One-off requests:** Recurring Wednesday orders, company-name lock, Pro Forma Invoice, Friday Statement of Account, address search, related-company pricing, customer complaint record and image catalogue.

**Later changes:** Later evidence moved Sales toward own-order entry, added pieces and variable box weights, elevated notifications, proposed a Driver role and then introduced a Tech alternative that bypasses Sales Order amendment by creating Delivery Notes directly from Pick Lists. No runner answer has yet settled these changes.

**3. Notifications and Reminders**

A notification is sent because something happened and someone else needs to know or act; a message shown because the user's own action is blocked belongs under Warnings and Blocking Rules.

**Section index:** NOTIF-01 Overdue Invoice · NOTIF-02 Near expiry · NOTIF-03 Submitted Sales Order · NOTIF-04 Draft Delivery Note · NOTIF-05 Blocked Sales Order · NOTIF-06 Price exception · NOTIF-07 Friday Statement of Account · NOTIF-08 Sunday sales summary.

**4. Warnings and Blocking Rules**

**Section index:** RULE-01 Credit-limit edit · RULE-02 Customer ownership · RULE-03 Unclear payment · RULE-04 Price boundary · RULE-05 Invoice quantity · RULE-06 Duplicate Invoice · RULE-07 Sales Order credit · RULE-08 Warehouse cost · RULE-09 Picked variance.

**4.1 RULE-01 --- Salesperson cannot change Customer credit limit**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** CJ, Ben or Arben, or Queenie is trying to change the credit limit on a Customer.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The account is using Sales User permission.\
**What MAIA does:** MAIA stops the change and leaves the credit limit read-only.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The Customer credit limit can be read but cannot be changed with Sales User permission.\
**What happens next:** The confirmed credit-limit owner changes it.\
**Why this rule is needed:** The client directly separated Sales reading from credit-limit maintenance.\
**Applies to:** Customer credit limit\
**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Basis:** Client-stated\
**Evidence:** E-028

**4.2 RULE-02 --- Customer access outside the assigned salesperson**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** A Sales User is trying to open a Customer assigned to another salesperson.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The explicit denial is not client-stated.\
**What MAIA does:** Unresolved --- see DECISION-16.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The final message depends on the Product classification and client answer.\
**What happens next:** No access is granted until confirmed.\
**Why this rule is needed:** SQL agent ownership is confirmed, but cross-visibility is not.\
**Applies to:** Customer\
**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026; Mindhive Daily Standup, 31 Jul 2026\
**Basis:** Derived and Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-030, E-032, E-096

**4.3 RULE-03 --- Unclear payment match requires Grace**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** Grace is trying to apply a Payment Receipt to an Invoice.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The payer name does not identify one clear Customer.\
**What MAIA does:** MAIA requires Grace to select the Customer before the Payment Receipt changes an Invoice balance.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The payer does not match one clear Customer and Finance must select it.\
**What happens next:** Grace selects the Customer and the Invoice or Invoices.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen receives payments from names that differ from Customer records.\
**Applies to:** Payment Receipt; Invoice\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Basis:** Client-stated\
**Evidence:** E-006, E-007

**4.4 RULE-04 --- Price outside the approved boundary**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** A Sales User is entering a price on a Quotation, Sales Order or Invoice.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The price is below the minimum, above the maximum or conflicts with a fixed price.\
**What MAIA does:** Unresolved --- see DECISION-20.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The final explanation depends on the selected intervention.\
**What happens next:** The final Price Controller action depends on the decision.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen directly stated minimum, maximum and fixed prices.\
**Applies to:** Quotation; Sales Order; Invoice\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Basis:** Derived from client-stated boundary\
**Evidence:** E-013

**4.5 RULE-05 --- Invoice quantity above Delivery Note quantity**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** Grace is trying to submit an Invoice.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The Invoice quantity exceeds the related Delivery Note quantity.\
**What MAIA does:** Product must confirm whether MAIA already stops this by default. See DECISION-26.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The Invoice quantity exceeds the delivered quantity.\
**What happens next:** Grace corrects the Invoice or Delivery Note after Product confirms the standard behaviour.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen said the Invoice must not exceed delivered quantity.\
**Applies to:** Invoice; Delivery Note\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Basis:** Client-stated outcome; Product classification Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-018

**4.6 RULE-06 --- Duplicate Invoice**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** Grace is trying to create an Invoice for a transaction that already has one.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** An existing Invoice is identified.\
**What MAIA does:** Product must confirm whether MAIA already stops this by default. See DECISION-26.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** An Invoice already exists for the transaction.\
**What happens next:** Grace opens the existing Invoice or corrects the source selection.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen wants to prevent duplicate billing.\
**Applies to:** Invoice\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Basis:** Client-stated outcome; Product classification Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-019

**4.7 RULE-07 --- Credit check on Sales Order**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** A Sales User is trying to submit a Sales Order.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The Customer fails the configured credit calculation.\
**What MAIA does:** Unresolved --- see DECISION-19, DECISION-07 and DECISION-04.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The final message depends on whether MAIA warns or stops.\
**What happens next:** The document follows the final Credit Controller decision if a stop is selected.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen requires payment discipline and one-time exceptions.\
**Applies to:** Sales Order\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026; Product-to-Tech Handoff Process Q&A, 27 and 31 Jul 2026\
**Basis:** Derived from client-stated credit practice; stage Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-016, E-017, E-091

**4.8 RULE-08 --- Warehouse cost and Purchasing visibility**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** Lai or a warehouse worker is opening an Item.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The account uses Logistics Manager or Logistics User permission.\
**What MAIA does:** Unresolved Product classification --- see DECISION-27.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** No client-specific warning text is approved.\
**What happens next:** Grant no cost or Purchasing access until Product classifies and the client confirms the restriction.\

**Basis:** Derived; Product classification required\

**4.9 RULE-09 --- Picked-quantity variance**

**Open rule details**

**What the user is trying to do:** Lai or a warehouse worker is entering the picked quantity on a Pick List.\
**When MAIA intervenes:** The difference from the ordered quantity exceeds a configurable variance.\
**What MAIA does:** Proposed only --- see DECISION-31.\
**What MAIA tells the user:** The final message depends on the selected variance and action.\
**What happens next:** The user follows the selected correction or approval path.\
**Why this rule is needed:** Variable-weight goods make quantity differences normal, but no client tolerance is evidenced.\
**Applies to:** Pick List\
**Source:** Product-to-Tech Handoff Process Q&A (Weiyon), 31 Jul 2026\
**Basis:** Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-005, E-092

**Suggested**

Where a credit or price decision is pending, keep the Sales Order in draft and show the named decision owner rather than letting the Sales User repeatedly resubmit it.

***This is a suggestion, not a confirmed client requirement.***

**5.4 AUTO-04 --- Apply a bulk Item Price and Price List file**

**What MAIA does:** MAIA shows the latest invoiced unit price as a reference.\
**What the user can see:** The Sales User sees the last price used.\

**Open automatic-action details**

**What MAIA does:** Internal design proposes the first available value, then blank.\
**What the user can see:** The Sales User sees the selected term or a blank field.\

**5.11 AUTO-11 --- Send confirmed documents to SQL**

**Open automatic-action details**

**When it happens:** When a Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice or Payment Receipt is confirmed.\
**Information used:** Confirmed document and SQL identifiers.\
**What MAIA does:** MAIA sends the supported fields to SQL.\
**What the user can see:** SQL reflects the transaction without separate re-entry.\

**5.12 AUTO-12 --- Keep Goods Receipt in SQL and use SQL stock**

**Open automatic-action details**

**When it happens:** When supplier goods arrive and when MAIA needs stock levels.\
**Information used:** Goods Receipt and stock information maintained in SQL.\
**What MAIA does:** Macro Frozen continues Goods Receipt in SQL; MAIA reads available stock information.\
**What the user can see:** Users see stock without a second supplier Goods Receipt in MAIA.\
**Why the client needs it:** The supplier process requires SQL supplier information.\
**Unsure:** Refresh timing, reconciliation and warehouse-code translation remain open.\
**Source:** Product Scope Gap Brief, 24 Jul 2026; Voice of Customer v3\
**Basis:** Derived\
**Evidence:** E-068

**5.13 AUTO-13 --- Create Delivery Notes directly from the confirmed Pick List**

**Open automatic-action details**

**When it happens:** When the Pick List is confirmed and Product selects the direct document path.\
**Information used:** Sales Orders, confirmed Pick List quantities and Customer delivery information.\
**What MAIA does:** MAIA creates the related Delivery Notes using actual picked quantities without amending submitted Sales Orders.\
**What the user can see:** Grace sees Delivery Notes with the picked quantity.\
**Why the client needs it:** Tech proposes removing an extra Sales Order amendment while preserving delivered and billed accuracy.\
**Unsure:** This is not client-confirmed and conflicts with AUTO-09. See DECISION-25.\
**Source:** Product-to-Tech Handoff Process Q&A (Weiyon), 31 Jul 2026\
**Basis:** Proposed\
**Evidence:** E-093

**Suggested**

When SQL Customer, Item or code matching fails, keep the affected document in draft with the original unmatched value visible and assign it to the initiating person.

***This is a suggestion, not a confirmed client requirement.***

**6.1.1 DECISION-25 --- Actual-quantity document path**

**Open decision**

**Question:** After a Pick List is confirmed, should MAIA (a) amend each Sales Order before creating Delivery Notes, or (b) create Delivery Notes directly from the Pick List without amending submitted Sales Orders?\
**Why it must be answered:** The answer changes the document path, permissions and testing for actual quantities.\
**Who should decide:** David with Grace and Lai, advised by Product and Tech\
**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-34; ROLE-37; AUTO-08; AUTO-09; AUTO-13\
**Evidence on each side:** E-005 confirms final-weight differences; E-058 derives Sales Order amendment; E-093 proposes direct Delivery Note creation.

**6.1.2 DECISION-03 --- Customer credit-limit owner**

**Open decision**

**Question:** Who may create and change a Customer credit limit: (a) CJ only, (b) Apple only, or (c) both with separate stated conditions?\
**Why it must be answered:** The same field cannot have unresolved ownership.\
**Who should decide:** David with Grace\
**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-10; ROLE-29; RULE-01\
**Evidence on each side:** E-028 denies ordinary Sales changes; E-029 discusses Sales Manager and Finance ownership.

**Who should decide:** David\
**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-04; ROLE-30; NOTIF-05; RULE-07\
